title: Disentangle, Align and Generalize: Learning A Timing Predictor from Different Technology Nodes
problem: Pre-routing timing prediction is critical for VLSI design, but accurate prediction at advanced technology nodes (7nm and below) is challenging because traditional ML methods require extensive training data that is time-consuming to prepare for each new technology node.
motivation: Accurate pre-routing timing prediction is paramount in VLSI design, but data scarcity and preparation overhead limit ML-based approaches for advanced technology nodes.
method: The framework uses transfer learning to leverage timing data from previous technology nodes for training on target nodes. It disentangles timing path features into node-agnostic and node-specific components, aligns these features across nodes to establish correspondences, and employs a Bayesian-based model to handle high variability in arrival times while enabling generalization to new designs.
key_novelty: Transfer learning framework that disentangles and aligns timing path features across technology nodes to overcome data scarcity in advanced node timing prediction.
contributions: Transfer learning approach for pre-routing timing prediction leveraging data from previous technology nodes
Feature disentanglement and alignment technique for handling cross-node timing variations
Bayesian model for handling high variability in arrival times and improving generalization to new designs
Experimental validation of transfer learning from 130nm to 7nm technology nodes

metrics.accuracy: effectiveness demonstrated but specific values not provided in abstract

limitations: Limitations and failure modes are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Transfer learning for cross-technology-node timing prediction
